say: Marjo Seki is an author and a teacher of Japanese cooking, based in Kouvola, Finland.
I designed and built a new website for Marjo through my company, Findaco.
The site has five pages, in Finnish.
A home page with Marjo's story,
cooking courses and services,
books,
upcoming events,
and a contact page.
The look is warm and playful, inspired by Japanese food culture:
soft colour bubbles, rounded photos, and clear type that works on any screen, from a phone to a desktop.
The client runs the site without me.
A small pencil icon opens a login,
and every text and image can then be edited right on the page.
One button publishes the changes.
The content is saved to GitHub,
Vercel rebuilds the site,
and the update is live in about a minute. No code, and no git knowledge needed.
Book orders and course enquiries go through small serverless functions, and arrive by email through Resend.
Passwords and API keys stay on the server, never in the browser.
Under the hood, it is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no framework,
so it loads fast and stays easy to maintain.

say.text: marjoseki.fi — a fast, friendly website that the client owns and runs.
